The source groups side-impact, rear-impact and rollover collisions in a statement requiring side-impact airbags for protection. The scope of that grouped equipment claim is unclear. Preserve the source assertion as typed debt rather than infer which current equipment protects in each collision type.

The enhanced-mirror paragraph on page 26 swaps left/right and edge terms, with about five inches of head movement and a rear fender about half an inch from the mirror bottom. Confirm the intended geometry instead of inventing a diagram.

Page 28 describes rear-facing infancy through at least age one and twenty pounds, a forward-facing toddler seat over age one and at least twenty pounds, a booster from ages four to eight when no taller than four feet nine inches, and adult-belt transition usually at eight or four feet nine inches. These are retained here as unconfirmed edition-bound claims; confirm current issuer recommendations before teaching them as safe transition cutoffs.
The broad airbag statement on page 27 must be interpreted only as front-airbag coverage, as clarified on page 28; vehicle-specific equipment comes from the owner manual.

Page 27 claims more than half of injury or fatal crashes occur below forty miles per hour and within twenty-five miles of home, without study provenance; withhold that statistical claim pending a dated official source.
